title: Laboratory: Critical Result Discrepancy — Hand-Typed vs Analyzer

fields.organization: Ottawa River Regional Medical Center — Laboratory
fields.summary: The LIS has returned to service but the interface engine ORRMC-INT01 remains non-functional, causing a one-way data flow. Manual entry of results from the analyzer is ongoing. A potassium result of 6.8 mmol/L for patient on 4 West was entered by lab tech after review of the analyzer printout. However, the paper record for the same test shows 4.2 mmol/L. The lab has no means to validate which value is correct. A second technician independently verified the analyzer output. The discrepancy is not attributable to instrument error. The lab is holding all critical results until the interface engine is restored.

findings.notes: LIS returned to service but interface engine not active; results not flowing to EHR
Printout for patient T-12 shows K+ 6.8 mmol/L, no visible error
Paper record for same test shows K+ 4.2 mmol/L; lab tech did not double-check input against printout
No second review performed before submission
No alert mechanism for 6.8 mmol/L K+ in EHR; alert not sent to provider
Logs show no calibration error or outlier for T-12
No independent review of hand-typed values before release
Patient T-12 (4 West) matches lab requisition and wristband
Specimen collected at 18:45, no signs of hemolysis
ORRMC-INT01 still not processing outgoing messages; still shows 'stuck' in logs

actionsTaken: Verified potassium result against analyzer printout and found agreement at 6.8 mmol/L
Notified HCC via phone at 19:50 that critical result discrepancy exists
Placed lab tech on standby to recheck all hand-typed critical results against printouts
Initiated second review for all lab results from 18:30 to 19:50
recommendations: Restore ORRMC-INT01 to full function within 2 hours to resolve data flow and prevent further split records
Implement mandatory second-person verification for all hand-typed critical results during EHR downtime
Assign a lab tech to 4 West to confirm potassium level at bedside and reconcile with EHR
Update EHR downtime procedures to include lab verification workflows under CNO oversight
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: IMG_0413-0417 (analyzer printout K+ 6.8, paper record K+ 4.2, lab tech review, HCC call log)

instructorNote: This inject tests the CNO’s ability to validate lab data under surge conditions and reinforce verification protocols. Watch for over-reliance on paper records or delayed action on critical values.
